scope: Pinned official Swift 6.4.3 / LLVM release option, normal Swift-to-Clang driver forwarding, module-lock implementation and exact private-cache applicability. No candidate/controller edit, compiler/native execution, Oracle observation, cache mutation or output-rule relaxation.

incidentAsReportedByRoot.observationScope: Root reported a symlink to the absolute same private-cache target, no other anomalies, exit -15 with forced cleanup and positive group absence. N did not repeat the census or independently read this raw incident receipt.

release.scopeLimit: The public release implementation is source provenance. These reads do not independently establish that every installed LLVM object was built from this exact commit.

sourceJoins.finding: The option is declared in the cc1 frontend section. BoolOption f/implicit-modules-use-lock marshals FrontendOpts.BuildingImplicitModuleUsesLock with DefaultTrue and a negative SetFalse. The exact negative spelling is -fno-implicit-modules-use-lock.
The boolean controls filesystem locking for implicit module builds and has an explicit true default.
Swift appends each -Xcc value in order to ClangImporterOptions.ExtraArgs.

The normal non-DirectClangCC1ModuleBuild path appends ExtraArgs to driver arguments and creates the Clang invocation through clang::createInvocation. The direct-cc1 route is a distinct configuration and is not proposed.

The driver explicitly forwards the value of each -Xclang argument to cc1. Whole-file lookup found no dedicated implicit_modules_use_lock forwarding. The proposal therefore uses explicit -Xclang, not an assumption that plain -Xcc forwards this cc1 option.

BuildingImplicitModuleUsesLock selects between compileModuleAndReadASTBehindLock and the same compileModuleAndReadASTImpl. False bypasses the lock wrapper; it does not skip compilation, AST validation or module-read errors.
The lock wrapper obtains ModuleCache's lock. The implementation explicitly treats this lock as duplicate-work coordination and already falls back to the same module implementation on lock errors.
CrossProcessModuleCache.prepareForGetLock creates the cache directory and getLock returns llvm::LockFileManager for the module filename.

tryLock makes the module name absolute, creates .lock-%%%%%%%%, writes owner host/PID metadata, and create_link publishes .lock to that unique name. An owned lock is removed by its destructor along with the unique file. This is a temporary lock protocol, not an admitted final PCM.
create_link tries create_symlink first and a hard link only on failure. This explains the artifact class reported by Root without treating that class as permitted output.
Nested module invocation copies the parent invocation and changes named module/output options; it does not reset BuildingImplicitModuleUsesLock.
resetNonModularOptions resets LangOptions, PreprocessorOptions and CodeGenOptions only, retaining the copied FrontendOptions lock boolean.

candidate.requiredApplicability: The cache is a newly owned private namespace used by the controller's serial phases, with no other admitted cache writer. Existing ownership/current-group/resource/output checks remain authoritative.

notProposed: No allowance for symlinks or hard links in any owned namespace.
No mutation or reuse of failed attempt2 output.

outcome: The narrow source-supported remedy is to suppress this implicit-module duplicate-work lock protocol for the existing private serial cache. The current regular-output rule can remain unchanged.
